===== [p69-69] FUNCTIONAL BEHAVIOR > • • READY TO RUN (= E40: WAITING FOR START) (1块) =====
--[p69]-- Input wafers of the process job are available (waiting at input location), the receipt of the first wafer may start after a ‘start process job’ command is received. This state is only applicable for lots for which the ‘process job pause’ attribute is set or for lots for which a pause command has been received while being in the QUEUED or PRE-PROCESSING state.

===== [p70-70] FUNCTIONAL BEHAVIOR > • • • Clear Unprocessed Wafers (1块) =====
--[p70]-- Remaining Wafers of the process job are moved out of the equipment without further processing. When additional wafers for this process job are provided by the track, these will be cycled out as well until the end-of-process job signal is received. Wafers are not being measured or exposed in this phase and should leave the equipment as efficient as possible.

===== [p52-52] FUNCTIONAL BEHAVIOR > • • • • READY CHECK (1块) =====
--[p52]-- The system status is being checked right before the first wafer is allowed to enter. If necessary due M-actions are triggered to achieve the appropriate processing conditions needed for production.

===== [p96-96] FUNCTIONAL BEHAVIOR > • • • • • ID VERIFICATION (1块) =====
--[p96]-- The barcode of the reticle is read and verified with the identification earlier received via a service or the reticle ID verification is waiting for host based verification.

===== [p87-87] FUNCTIONAL BEHAVIOR > WAFER LOCATION States (1块) =====
--[p87]-- • UNOCCUPIED
The wafer location does not hold a wafer.
• OCCUPIED
The wafer Location holds a wafer.

===== [p104-104] FUNCTIONAL BEHAVIOR > • POD SLOT MAP STATUS (1块) =====
--[p104]-- Shows the actual status of the Pod with respect to the slot map. There are 4 possible states:

===== [p70-70] FUNCTIONAL BEHAVIOR > • STOPPED (1块) =====
--[p70]-- Processing of the process job has been stopped and all wafers belonging to the process job are cycled out of the machine. Stopped lots are considered being removed from the active queue.

===== [p69-69] FUNCTIONAL BEHAVIOR > • • • CURRENT (1块) =====
--[p69]-- The first wafer belonging to this process job has entered exposure position. Without interrupts the process job remains in this state until the last Wafer of the process job has been exposed.

===== [p111-112] Appendix A Application Examples on how to use Objects (3块) =====
--[p112]-- If this top directory (user\_data/RDM) is not specified in the recipe identifier, it is assumed to precede the recipe identifier. So user\_data/RDM/recipe\_01, refers to the same recipe as recipe\_01.
--[p111]-- “ContentMap”
The order of the list is exactly the same as the order of the lotqueue reflected in the GUI.
Example 7 Request all attributes for recipe ‘recipe\_01’:
S14F1 L,5 1. ““ 2. “MRCP” 3. L,1 1. “recipe\_01” 4. L,0 5. L,0
The recipe identifier must include any directory information if applicable; user\_data/RDM is the top directory under which all recipes are stored (including subdirectories).
--[p111]-- This section shows some examples (queries) on how to use objects.
Example 1 Query the location of all reticles present in the tool:
S14F1 L,5 1. ““ 2. “RETICLE” 3. L,1 1. “4A00234” 4. L,0 5. L,0
Example 4 Query the Contentmap for reticle pod 1 and pod 2. Assume that the ObjIDs for the pods are “POD 1” and “POD 2”:
S14F1 L,5 1. ““ 2. “RETICLEPOD” 3. L,2 1. “POD 1” 2. “POD 2” 4. L,0 5. L,1 1. “ContentMap”
Example 5 Query the Recipe Name of a process job called “LOT01”:

===== [p49-108] Description (13块) =====
--[p105]-- This single message is used to Create Multiple Process Jobs. Each of the jobs can be unique in its association of material to the process recipe. Please see Table 6.19, “Message Detail PRJobCreateEnh,” on page 590 for a description of the process job parameters. The number of process jobs that can be downloaded is limited by the maximum number of process jobs the process job queue can hold and limited by the T3-timer setting on the host system.
--[p105]-- Each process job in the S16F15 will be validated before it will be added to the process job queue. The time it takes to validate a process job depends on the parameters that are specified in the process job. After all process jobs in the S16F15 are validated, the reply message S16F16 will be send back to the host system. The host system should therefor guard that no more process jobs are in the S16F15 than can be validated by the TWINSCAN within the T3-timer setting of the host system.
--[p78]-- This message is used to request that a given set of attributes be assigned specified values for all objects of the specified type and exactly matching the specified attribute requirements. Certain attributes may not be changed through the interface. For a description of filters see S14F1.
--[p87]-- The number of values that the Process Job Milestones can assume is limited, but the conditions under which a process job can meet one of these milestones is different. A Job can for example reach the Job Complete status because the Process was Aborted.
--[p49]-- The host links a number of reports to an event (CEID). The event reports are set to disabled when they are linked by default. This means that the occurrence of an event does not cause the report to be sent immediately. The report has to be enabled first. See S2F37 for enabling reports.
--[p79]-- This message is used to request that the object specified in OBJSPEC be deleted. The list of attribute settings depends upon the type of object to be deleted.
--[p79]-- This message is used to acknowledge that the attributes for the specified objects have been set as requested or to indicate an error for each attribute value that is not set as requested. The order of attributes is retained from the primary message.
--[p57]-- The host requests the equipment to write data to a tag. The reticle pod must be indicated either by its location or its identifier, or both. DATASEG may be used to indicate a specific section of the data to be written or overwritten. DATALENGTH may be used to indicate the length of the data to be written.
--[p57]-- This message is used to return requested information from the tag of the reticle pod indicated in the request and to acknowledge the results of the requests.
--[p77]-- This message is used to transfer the set of requested attributes for the specified object(s). The order of attributes is retained from the primary message. See “Application Examples on how to use Objects” on page 612.
--[p80]-- This message is used to acknowledge the success or failure of deleting the object specified. The list of attributes returned is dependent upon the type of object to be deleted.
--[p108]-- Acknowledge the request to de-queue and report any errors. PRJOBID will contain the identifier of any jobs that were successfully de-queued. ERRTEXT will contain the identifier of any jobs that were not de-queued.
Exception
--[p84]-- If SVCACK = 0, the service is accepted and completed immediately. The parameters required for response are listed in the message.

===== [p36-37] Completion Events (5块) =====
--[p36]-- In general an acknowledge code in the secondary message informs the host about the outcome of a service request. Most services are performed immediately, some services take time to complete. The completion of a service can be monitored via collection events (S6F11), and in two cases (MoveReticle and Re-qualifiyReticle) via completion messages (S14F21). In this section a table of completion events is presented for every command that is available to the host.

There are two types of SECS messages:
• Primary messages
These are the first part of the transaction. They are questions and requests. They are the odd numbered functions.
• Secondary messages
These are the second part of the transaction. They are answers and replies. They are the even numbered functions.
The general message description layout is:

===== [p63-64] Multi-block Grant (MBG) (3块) =====

===== [p74-75] Stream 9: System Errors (5块) =====
--[p74]-- This stream provides a method of informing the host that a received message block cannot be handled, or that a timeout on a transaction (receive) timer has occurred. The messages indicate either Message Faults or Communications Faults, but they do not indicate Communications Failures.
• Message Fault
A Message Fault occurs when the system receives a message which it cannot process because of a fault that arises from the content, context, or length of the message.
• Communications Fault
--[p74 [表]]-- A Communications Fault occurs when the system does not receive an expected message (when a transaction timer or a conversation timer has expired).
• Communications Failure
In the event of a Communications Failure, no Stream 9 message is sent.
S9F0 | Abort Transaction (S9F) S,H← E
S9F1 | Same form as S1F0.
Unrecognized Device ID (UDN) S,H← E
Description | The device ID in the message block header did not correspond to any known device ID in the node detecting the error.

===== [p80-80] Generic Service Request (GSR) M,H → E Reply (2块) =====
--[p80]-- This identification is used in every delayed completion information of a time consuming service.
The OPID is zero only if the service does not take a long time.
The OBJSPEC specifies the object instance except where the original service standards allow specific objects. OBJSPEC can specify the owner object.
The other data items are mapped from the service request parameter list of the applied object service.
--[p80]-- The host requests an object to do the specified service with its associated parameters. Multi-block is preceded by the S14F23/F24 multi-block Inquire/Grant transaction.
Each message is given a unique DATAID. For example, each message from the multi-block Inquire transaction has a unique DATAID.
The OPID is an identification that is given by the host as a parameter to the service. This identification is used in every delayed completion information of a time consuming service.
